▌ v0.4.1 · Go runtime · MIT

Terminal UIs,
written as text.

Tuimark is a view language for terminals. Structure lives in .tui markup, style in .tcss, data in JSON, and behavior in named actions. A small Go runtime lays it out on a cell grid, paints it, and dumps every frame as JSON, so a coding agent can check what it built without ever looking at a screen.

Get started →For coding agentsGitHub
$go install github.com/abdul-hamid-achik/tuimark/cmd/tuimark@latest
is / is not
  • ✓ interpreted at run time: nothing generates Go
  • ✓ a closed catalog: 24 tags, 35 properties
  • ✓ integer cells, grapheme-aware widths
  • ✓ deterministic dumps you can diff and golden-test
  • ✗ no pixels, no expressions, no logic in markup
  • ✗ not a wrapper around another TUI framework
the language →

Three files, one frame.

A list bound to an array, a detail pane bound to the selection, key hints built from the keymap, and a media query that stacks the panes on a narrow terminal. 

<tui theme="dark">
  <style src="theme.tcss"/>
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="q" action="quit" label="quit"/>
    <bind keys="enter" action="open" when="#tickets:focus" label="open"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="main" focus="#tickets">
    <row id="body">
      <list id="tickets" title="tickets" each="tickets as t" key="t.id"
            bind="selected" on:select="preview">
        <item>
          <text>{t.id} {t.title}</text>
        </item>
      </list>
      <box id="detail" title="{current.id}">
        <text wrap="wrap">{current.body}</text>
      </box>
    </row>
    <hints id="keys"/>
  </screen>
</tui>

$ tuimark dump app.tui --data sample.json --cols 80

Built for the agent loop.

An agent cannot see a terminal. Tuimark gives it the frame as data instead, and a briefing, tuimark agents, generated from the runtime's own catalogs so it never drifts.

  1. 1 editapp.tui · theme.tcss · sample.json

    Markup, a reduced CSS, and JSON. No Go in the view.

  2. 2 validatetuimark validate app.tui --data sample.json

    Every problem is a code: V parse, L layout, B bind.

  3. 3 dumptuimark dump app.tui --data sample.json --cols 80 --rows 10 --format json

    The frame as data: the grid, every node’s rect, the errors.

  4. 4 playtuimark play app.tui --data sample.json --cols 80 --rows 10 --input "down enter"

    Replay keys, typing and clicks with no terminal; read which actions fired.

A vocabulary you can hold in your head.

The catalog is closed. An unknown tag is V001, not a new widget; an unknown property is V003. version="2" documents add 6 tags (marked ²) and the rest of the 0.2 vocabulary; version="1" documents keep their exact meaning.

document
  • <tui>
  • <style>
  • <keymap>
  • <bind>
  • <screen>
layout
  • <col>
  • <row>
  • <box>
  • <scroll>
  • <spacer>
  • <tabs>2
  • <tab>2
content
  • <text>
  • <rule>
  • <sparkline>2
  • <hints>2
interactive
  • <list>
  • <item>
  • <input>
  • <button>
  • <progress>

Real apps, same few files.

Every example in the repository is a .tui, a .tcss, and sample data, with an optional Go host.

monitor studio · grid, gauges, sparklinescoding-agent chat · transcript, tools, approvalsinbox · search, list, detail, @media

All examples →

The host is a few lines of Go.

It loads the document, binds data, and answers named actions. Layout, focus, keys, the mouse, colors, and terminal handling stay in the runtime.

main.go
ui, err := tuimark.Load("app.tui")
if err != nil {
	return err
}
_ = ui.Bind("", data) // the JSON store
ui.On("preview", func(ev tuimark.Event) error {
	return ui.Set("current", lookup(ev.Keys["t"]))
})
ui.On("open", openTicket)
return ui.Run(os.Stdout)
the whole API
  • Loadread a .tui file
  • Parseread one from an io.Reader
  • Bindput data in the store
  • Setchange it while running
  • Onhandle a named action
  • Cataloglist the actions used
  • Dumprender a frame to JSON
  • Validatelist the diagnostics
  • Rundrive the terminal

Install.

Then run tuimark agents and hand the output to your agent.

Install the CLI with Go

One static binary, no CGO. It lands in $(go env GOPATH)/bin; make sure that is on your PATH.

$go install github.com/abdul-hamid-achik/tuimark/cmd/tuimark@latest
